findings.finding: The base year-1 price of 288$ (+212%) is not caused by mis-scaled inputs. The inputs check out against their sources: current-year revenue 3,378M = 9M reported 2,363.3M + Q4 guide midpoint 1,015M (1,000-1,030M, release 2026-10-29). FY2027 base 4,222.8M (+25%) is only about 4% above the Q4-guide run rate of 4.06B. Operating margin after SBC is 30.2% in FY2027, against 29.4% TTM (908.0M / 3,088.9M). SBC is 11.9% of revenue, against 12.5% TTM. Tax is 22%, against 2% reported (valuation allowance). Shares are 193.1M (cover 2026-10-28). That gives FY2027 EPS 5.48, i.e. 16.8x at 92.2 (trailing 17.9x = 17.8B / 991.7M TTM net income at a 2% tax rate). The jump has three causes. (1) Construction: the yearly row is value_t = the economics multiple x next-year EPS, so year 1 assumes the whole gap between price and model closes within 12 months: 43.1x on FY2028 EPS 6.69 = 288. The year-0 economics value is already 267.5. (2) The economics multiple of 43-49x comes from roic 0.95 held through the terminal, 16 explicit years with growth fading from 22% to 5%, and a terminal spread of only 2.9 points (Ke_T 7.86% minus g_T 4.98% = risk-free, an engine convention). That spread alone gives a terminal P/E of about 33x. (3) The price 92.2 is a one-day post-results level: prior close 129.6, so -29% in a day, and the snapshot is extended-hours (see trace). It is not a long-run average.
findings.where: companies/RDDT/out/casefile.json company_path.scenarios.base.economics (values year 0-1, multiple_path, terminal_cost_of_equity 0.078557, terminal_growth 0.0498); out/table_he.md yearly table row 'שנה 1'
findings.fix: No input change is needed for scaling. In delivery, state next to the table that year 1 is the full re-rating to the model's value, not a forecast of a +212% move in one year. Also state that the multiple rests on a 2.9-point terminal spread and a 95% return on capital held for good. Show the 5-year CAGR (base about +33%/yr from 92.2) as the comparable figure.

findings.finding: The DCF fair value (211) and the yearly path (year-0 economics value 267.5, 27% higher) use inconsistent reinvestment. The forecast charges growth_capex_pct of 12.5% of revenue in FY2027 and 10.9% in FY2028 (about 552M against NOPAT of about 1.22B: a reinvestment rate of about 45%, implying an incremental ROIC of about 44%). Its terminal ROIC is 0.24 (engine_terminal_roic). The company_path base uses roic 0.95, and the bull uses 1.30. The table lists 'ההשקעה הנדרשת לכל דולר מכירות נוסף' and 'התשואה על ההון לטווח הארוך' as engine-rule levers, while the path's ROIC is evidenced. Own history supports the high figure: operating capital (equity minus cash and securities) went from 452M at FY2025 (2,929.0 - 953.6 - 1,523.2) to 579.7M at Q3 2026, while operating income went from 442.0M to 908.0M TTM. That is an incremental after-tax return well above 100%, and capex is 6.7M a year. So the DCF is the more conservative of the two because it runs on engine rules, not company data.
findings.where: casefile fc.paths.base growth_capex_pct; company_path.scenarios.base.economics.roic 0.95 vs engine_terminal_roic 0.2399 (roic_minus_engine_terminal_roic 0.71); fc.driver_gaps / table row 'הנחות בלי נתון של החברה'
findings.fix: Repair (optional but preferred): add an evidenced sales-to-capital or growth_capex override from own history (capex about 0.2% of revenue; receivables growth as the main reinvestment) so the DCF and the path share one reinvestment basis. Otherwise state in delivery that the fair value 211 uses engine-default reinvestment, and that the path uses a 95% evidenced return, which is why they differ.

findings.finding: Ownership uses 193.09M basic cover shares with zero incremental dilutive shares (assumption 'dilution': convertibles/warrants status 'missing'). Q3 2026 diluted weighted shares were 201.86M (nm_shares_diluted_wavg_q_2026_09_30), and management cites 206.3M fully diluted (call 2026-10-29). Existing vested in-the-money options and RSUs are already-granted claims, not future SBC, so the sbc_pct charge does not cover them. Per-share values (fair value 211, entry price 180, every yearly price) are overstated by roughly 4-7%.

findings.fix: Repair: set the dilution to the treasury-method dilutive shares from the 10-Q equity note (outstanding options and RSUs at 92.2), or at least to 201.86M - 193.09M = 8.8M as an evidenced proxy citing nm_shares_diluted_wavg_q_2026_09_30 and pf_10q_20261030, then rerun ticker-value.

findings.finding: The bull multiple is far above the company's own history. The bull economics multiple is 91.1x forward at year 0 and 72.8x at year 1, against own_history trailing P/E of low 18.7, median 40.3 and high 55.6 (2026-02 to 2026-10). It rests on roic 1.30, the TTM average return on operating capital, held through the terminal for 15+ years. The roic_above_100pct flag is correctly a decimal: the evidence is NOPAT of about 717M on 579.7M of operating capital, i.e. 124% ('ROIC CHECK' note), not a percent typed as a number. Holding it forever, on a capital base that is small mainly because the cash pile is excluded, is still a peak-level assumption. The base year-1 multiple of 43.1x is also above the own-history median, on a stock that trades at 16.8x forward.
findings.where: casefile company_path.scenarios.bull.economics (roic 1.3, multiple_path[0..1] 91.1, 72.8); company_path.flags roic_above_100pct; position/path.json own_history
findings.fix: Say in delivery that the bull prices a multiple above anything in the stock's own history. Optionally fade the bull roic toward the base value in the terminal, or cap the bull's year-1-5 multiple near the own-history high (55.6x) with the reason recorded.

findings.finding: Tax at 22% from FY2027 is conservative for cash earnings. The 10-Q says the full US valuation allowance may be released within 12 months, which implies sizeable deferred tax assets (NOLs and credits) that would keep cash taxes below 22% for some years. A release would be a one-time GAAP gain and is correctly kept out of recurring EPS.

findings.fix: Note only. Optionally record the NOL and credit carryforward amounts from the 10-K tax note as an upside lever. Do not change the recurring rate without the note's figures.
